title: Event schema stability & deprecation playbook (v0.1)
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines stability tiers for audit event fields, a deprecation policy and rollout playbook aimed at minimizing downstream breakage (SIEMs, evidence automation jobs, compliance reports) as we iterate the audit/event schema from v1 -> v2 -> v3. It is intentionally pragmatic: preserve backwards compatibility for common consumers, and provide a clear migration path and observability during transitions.

Background and motivation:
- We currently have several ad-hoc schema changes that caused consumer regressions in customer SIEM exports and evidence automation pipelines.
- Need to reduce emergency migrations and provide repeatable communication and tooling for change.
- This doc complements the event-taxonomy and audit-contract notes (see linked artifacts) by focusing on lifecycle and operational controls.

High-level approach:
1) Semantic-style versioning for the audit contract (major.minor.build). Major increments (1.x -> 2.0) indicate potential breaking changes to stable fields. Minor increments add non-breaking fields or mappings. Build increments are internal refinements (formatting, docs).
2) Field-level stability tiers (Stable | Guarded | Experimental).
   - Stable: guaranteed for the lifetime of a major version. No renames, type changes, or removal without a major version bump.
   - Guarded: allowed for additive changes and non-breaking enrichments; removal/rename requires 1) 3-month deprecation notice and 2) telemetry that consumers have not relied on the field for >90% of recorded reads.
   - Experimental: may change or be removed with no notice; intended for early pilot features.

Field-level rules (examples):
- event.id (Stable): UUID, always present.
- event.type (Stable): enum text; new enum members may be added in minor versions.
- actor.user_id (Guarded): string|null; attempts to restrict changes. Renames require deprecation.
- metadata.request_packet (Experimental): freeform blob.

Deprecation policy and timeline:
- Deprecation announcement: post Confluence page + Slack #sec-announce + tagged Jira epic. Minimum 90 days before removal when deprecating Guarded fields.
- Deprecated-but-supported window: 90 days. During this window we:
  * Emit a new diagnostic event (audit.schema.deprecation_notice) for each use of the deprecated field.
  * Add a header in exported SIEM feeds (see SIEM mapping section) indicating deprecated fields exist.
  * Run weekly telemetry on consumer usage (by client_id, route, and external export destinations).
- Removal: earliest allowed at day 91 from announcement, gated on: telemetry showing <10 active consumers (configurable) or explicit migration confirmation from large consumers.

Semantic-versioned change examples (v1 -> v2):
- Safe minor(add): add "request.geo.country" (minor version). Consumers that ignore unknown fields are unaffected.
- Guarded rename(remove) example: rename "actor.user" -> "actor.user_id": announce and add both fields for 90 days, emit deprecation diagnostic events when both are present, then remove old field at v2.0.

SIEM export considerations:
- SIEM consumers often expect flat, strongly-typed fields. We maintain a stable SIEM mapping layer: the gateway that converts nested audit events into flattened SIEM documents. Changes to nested schema must include mapping updates and a compatibility shim for downstream exports for the full 90-day deprecation window.
- For high-volume exports, binary-compatibility is a hard requirement: add new fields only (no renames) during the supported window.

RBAC-sensitive and PII handling:
- Fields that contain PII (actor.email, request.ip, request.payload) are marked as Guarded. Default export policy will mask PII for non-authorized export destinations.
- RBAC v2 integration: mapping between RBAC roles and export rights lives in the private-deployments control-plane. Any schema change that alters PII location must trigger an access review and a security test checklist.

Evidence automation hooks:
- Evidence collectors (for audits, e-discovery) must continue to function during deprecation windows. We will:
  * Provide an adapter layer in the evidence automation service that reads both old and new fields where applicable.
  * Surface a weekly migration report listing evidence archives created using deprecated fields.

Observability and telemetry requirements for any schema change:
- Add a new schema-change event to the audit stream listing changed fields, change author, target major/minor version.
- Emit per-field usage counters (per client_id) for at least 120 days after a change is announced.
- Create a dashboard in Console: "Audit schema migrations" showing number of active consumers, downstream exports affected, and deprecation diagnostic event counts.

Migration playbook (step-by-step):
1) Draft change and propose in "#sec-schema" channel + post Confluence draft (owner assigns Jira).
2) Add stability tier tags to each field in the proposal.
3) Run internal compatibility test suite against sample SIEM exports and evidence automation jobs.
4) Create migration adaptors (if rename/remove) and deploy a dual-write shim that writes both old and new fields for the 90-day window.
5) Announce deprecation (Confluence + Slack + email to known integrators) and start telemetry collection.
6) Weekly migration check-ins; escalate to integrators with >1% usage of deprecated fields.
7) After the window and gating checks, remove field and increment major version if breaking.

Minimal consumer migration example (rename actor.user -> actor.user_id):
- Phase 0 (proposal): add actor.user_id in v1.1, dual-write from service.
- Phase 1 (90-day deprecation): emit audit.schema.deprecation_notice when actor.user is present; run adaptor for evidence automation to read both.
- Phase 2 (removal): drop actor.user and bump to v2.0.

Compatibility test checklist (pre-release):
- Unit tests for serializer/deserializer for stable fields.
- SIEM export acceptance tests: ensure flattened mapping still emits expected headers and types.
- Evidence automation regression tests: ingest test archives containing both old and new fields.
- RBAC access regression: verify masking rules still apply post-change.

Changelog notes (working):
- v1.0 (baseline): original schema; stable fields defined.
- v1.1 (minor): added request.geo.* fields; added schema diagnostic event.
- v2.0 (planned): rename actor.user -> actor.user_id; remove legacy request_id format; tighten PII masking defaults.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Telemetry retention for field-level usage: 120 days vs 180 days? Longer retention helps long-tail integrators but increases storage.
- Exact gating thresholds for removal (10 active consumers is a starting heuristic).
- Who signs off for enterprise customers that request extended support windows?

Appendix A — example diagnostic event (stringified):
{
  "event": "audit.schema.deprecation_notice",
  "deprecated_field": "actor.user",
  "replacement": "actor.user_id",
  "announced_at": "2025-11-03T14:00:00Z",
  "detected_in_event_id": "<event.id>"
}

Appendix B — rollout checklist (short):
- [ ] Confluence doc published
- [ ] Jira epic created + owners assigned
- [ ] Dual-write shims deployed
- [ ] SIEM mapping compatibility tests green
- [ ] Evidence automation adapters deployed
- [ ] Consumer announcement sent
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards live

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a draft intended to align engineering, security, product, and customer-facing teams on low-friction schema evolution. Feedback: add concrete thresholds for gating and propose a person/team for final sign-off on removals.
